summary: The bill amends the Small Business Act to create a new 5% governmentwide goal for prime and subcontract awards to veteran-owned small businesses, authorize sole-source awards and veteran-only competitions above the simplified acquisition threshold, and update reporting, oversight, and program rules to track and support that participation.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends federal contracting rules under the Small Business Act to create new sole-source and set-aside authorities plus a 5% governmentwide goal specifically for veteran-owned small businesses. These changes alter how existing procurement dollars are allocated but do not increase or decrease total federal outlays or authorize new spending programs. Therefore the bill has no net effect on the level of government spending.
The legislation contains no tax provisions, credits, deductions, or rate changes.
No provisions address health insurance, providers, Medicare/Medicaid, or any aspect of the healthcare system.
The bill is silent on firearms, background checks, or gun-related regulations.
No immigration, visa, border, or refugee provisions appear in the text.
The bill does not mention reproductive health services or abortion access.
While the measure benefits veteran-owned firms, it does not alter defense budget levels, procurement accounts, or military spending authorizations.
No environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions are present.
The legislation does not modify any welfare, nutrition, housing, or income-support programs.
No education funding, school-choice, or federal education policy changes are included.
The bill contains nothing related to controlled substances, enforcement, or decriminalization.
No sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform measures are present.
The text does not address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
Because the bill neither authorizes new spending nor reduces existing outlays, it has no measurable impact on deficits or the debt trajectory.
No provisions touch on LGBTQ protections, nondiscrimination rules, or related civil-rights matters.
Foreign assistance programs are not mentioned.
The legislation is unrelated to voting access, election administration, or campaign finance.
No data-privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance provisions exist.
The bill does not alter labor standards, collective-bargaining rights, or union-related rules.
No religious-exemption or civil-rights language appears in the measure.
